BiblicalUsage: Daniel is the prophet of the exile who purposed in his heart not to defile himself, and God gave him favour. His name appears when the king's decree threatens the wise men of Babylon, when Belshazzar clothes him in scarlet for reading the writing on the wall, and when his visions leave him troubled to the end of the book. He is the man who prayed with his windows open toward Jerusalem and was thrown to the lions for it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Daniel is the pattern for the believer in a foreign land: resolve first, pray openly, and trust God with the lions. My position is that faithfulness in small things, like a meal, is what prepares a man for the den.
RelatedEvents: Daniel in the Lions' Den; Daniel's Resolve in Babylon
